newsitem.title: FRANCE: France criticises Azerbaijan separatist election.
newsitem.headline: France criticises Azerbaijan separatist election.

text.p: France criticised the breakaway Caucasus region of Nagorno-Karabakh on Friday for holding a presidential election, saying the poll would affect talks on its claim of independence from Azerbaijan.
"France deplores this initiative," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said, referring to the election plan.

"The so-called 'presidential elections' by the self-proclaimed leaders of Nagorno-Karabakh, set for November 24, can only complicate the situation," spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a routine ministry briefing.
He appealed to all the parties to show a willingness to compromise and goodwill in order to reach a lasting solution.
The mountainous Caucasus region, a patchwork of more than 60 ethnic groups, has been torn by wars since the break-up of the Soviet Union.
Nagorno-Karabakh is a predominantly Armenian enclave that is legally part of Azerbaijan.
Azerbaijan and Armenia fought a bitter war from 1988-94. A shaky ceasefire forged after sweeping Armenian gains left Azerbaijan without Karabakh and a swathe of territory around it.
Karabakh has made no secret of its desire to join Armenia. But Azerbaijan refuses to consider anything more than autonomy for the region.

Rummelhardt said a solution to the conflict should respect the territorial integrity of Azerbaijan and grant considerable autonomy for Nagorno-Karabakh while assuring respect for human rights and the right of refugees to return home.
